statement: The function returns a result r, and r equals the number of pairs (i, j) of integers such that 0 <= i <= j < n and the contiguous non-empty subarray nums[i..j] (that is, nums[i], nums[i+1], ..., nums[j]) has exactly as many distinct values as the whole array nums. Equivalently, letting D = |{nums[k] : 0 <= k < n}|, r = |{(i, j) : 0 <= i <= j < n and |{nums[k] : i <= k <= j}| = D}|.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 2000.

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail, panic, or overflow) for every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 2000.

statement: The returned r satisfies r >= 1. Moreover, the whole array nums[0..n-1] is complete, because its set of distinct values is exactly the set of distinct values of nums.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 2000.

statement: The function returns r = n * (n + 1) / 2. Equivalently, every contiguous non-empty subarray of nums is complete.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 2000, and the whole array has exactly one distinct value (D = |{nums[k] : 0 <= k < n}| = 1).

statement: The function returns r = 1; the only complete subarray is the whole array nums[0..n-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 2000, and the entries of nums are pairwise distinct (D = |{nums[k] : 0 <= k < n}| = n).

statement: Let D = |{nums[k] : 0 <= k < n}|. The returned r satisfies r <= (n - D + 1) * (n - D + 2) / 2, which is the number of contiguous non-empty subarrays of nums whose length is at least D.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 2000.

statement: For every 0 <= i <= j < n, the subarray nums[i..j] is complete with respect to nums if and only if the subarray nums'[i..j] is complete with respect to nums'. Consequently, the returned value r for nums equals the value returned by count_complete_subarrays on nums'.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 2000. Let nums' be any array of length n satisfying 1 <= nums'[i] <= 2000 for all i and having the same equality pattern as nums: for all 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, nums[i] = nums[j] if and only if nums'[i] = nums'[j].

statement: Let rev be the array defined by rev[k] = nums[n - 1 - k] for 0 <= k < n. For every 0 <= i <= j < n, nums[i..j] is complete in nums if and only if rev[n - 1 - j .. n - 1 - i] is complete in rev. Consequently, the returned r for nums equals the number of complete subarrays of rev.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 2000.

statement: The function returns r = p * q.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 2000. Suppose there exist positive integers p and q with p + q = n and two distinct values a and b such that nums[i] = a for 0 <= i < p and nums[i] = b for p <= i < n.

statement: The function returns r = n * (n - 1) / 2. Equivalently, the complete subarrays are exactly the contiguous subarrays of length at least 2.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 2000. Suppose the whole array has exactly two distinct values (D = |{nums[k] : 0 <= k < n}| = 2) and no two adjacent entries are equal: for every i with 0 <= i < n - 1, nums[i] != nums[i + 1].
